title: Dutch Apple Crumb Pie
source: King Arthur, Smitten Kitchen (crumb), Food & Wine (buttermilk), adapted

items.body: Whisk the flour and salt in a bowl. Add the butter, in ½ in dice, and rub it in with your fingertips until the biggest lumps are pea-size.

Stir it into the bowl with a fork. Squeeze a handful: if it holds, stop, even if shaggy. Crumbles? Add 1 tsp at a time, 1 tbsp more at most; extra liquid makes it leathery. Flatten into a disk without kneading, wrap, and refrigerate ≥30 min.
In a second bowl, whisk the brown sugar and granulated sugar into the melted butter until smooth.
Stir the flour and salt into the butter mixture until no dry flour shows. Press it into the bowl and cool until firm, 10–15 min.
Break it into ½–¾ in chunks, leaving some smaller. Bigger chunks stay soft in the middle. Spread on a plate or quarter sheet pan and refrigerate at least 30 min.

Rack in the lowest position, oven to 425 °F (218 °C). On a lightly floured counter, roll the chilled dough to a 13 in round. Fit it into the pie plate, crimp a high rim, and refrigerate it while you do the apples.

ings.name: Apples, Granny Smith + Golden Delicious
ings.note: half and half; peeled, cored, sliced

items.body: Weigh the sliced apples into a large bowl. Add the sugar, flour, cinnamon and nutmeg, and toss until every slice is coated. Pile it all into the chilled shell, including whatever is left in the bowl, and mound the middle.
Scatter all the cold crumb chunks over the apples; don’t press them in. Set the pie on the half sheet pan to catch drips. Bake at 425 °F (218 °C) for 15 min.

Lower the oven to 350 °F (177 °C). Bake ≈1–1½ h more, until juice bubbles up through the crumb in the center, a skewer slides easily through the apples, and the bottom looks golden brown through the glass. Still pale underneath? Keep going. Once the crumb is deep golden, cover it loosely with foil.
Cool on a rack until lukewarm, at least 1 h, before slicing.

nutritionSource: USDA FoodData Central: SR Legacy (apples without skin, sugar, brown sugar, unsalted butter, buttermilk, cinnamon, nutmeg) and Branded Foods labels (King Arthur All-Purpose, Morton). Buttermilk counted at 3 tbsp; ice water is ≈2 kcal and 8 mg a slice less. Flour for the counter not counted.
notes: Built from King Arthur’s crust and filling and Smitten Kitchen’s crumb. Buttermilk instead of water won Food & Wine’s six-way crust test, 10/10 to 9/10. First bake, 2026-11-08: the filling set to a perfect jelly after ≈1 h at 350 °F (177 °C), but extra ice water and the lower-middle rack gave a leathery crust. King Arthur: less liquid makes a more tender crust, and glass belongs on the bottom rack. Go by the cues, not the clock.
Half tart and half sweet works best and holds its shape. Braeburn or Jonagold can replace the Golden Delicious.
Keeps 2 days at room temp, loosely covered; the fridge softens the crumb. To recrisp, 300 °F (149 °C) for 15–20 min, not the microwave.
